pages.quiz:
INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #14
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which is a verb in: The pot tipped over? (1 mark)
   A. over
   B. The
   C. pot
   D. tipped

2. Which adjective describes shape? (1 mark)
   A. loud
   B. heavy
   C. round
   D. red

3. Which is a good tip for reciting? (1 mark)
   A. Look at the audience and speak clearly
   B. Cover your face
   C. Look at the floor and mumble
   D. Speak very fast

4. What is the best way to check the order of your paragraph? (1 mark)
   A. Read it aloud
   B. Copy it
   C. Fold the page
   D. Cover it

5. Which adjective describes size? (1 mark)
   A. soft
   B. tiny
   C. round
   D. red

6. How long should each line in a dialogue usually be? (1 mark)
   A. Short, like real speech
   B. None
   C. One page
   D. Very long speeches

7. Which is a proverb? (1 mark)
   A. Please sit down
   B. A stitch in time saves nine
   C. Bring your book
   D. It is Monday

8. Which is a signal word for the second step? (1 mark)
   A. Never
   B. Finally
   C. Yesterday
   D. Next

9. Which interjection shows disgust? (1 mark)
   A. Bravo
   B. Aha
   C. Hurray
   D. Yuck

10. What is a portfolio of proverbs? (1 mark)
   A. A game
   B. A poem
   C. A kind of bag for money
   D. A folder where proverbs are collected and kept

11. Which pair of verbs shows an action? (1 mark)
   A. table, chair
   B. is, are
   C. vote, count
   D. red, blue

12. Where should the comma go in I have money and I want a book? (1 mark)
   A. After want
   B. After have
   C. After I
   D. Before and

13. Why should you not invent interjections for your mother tongue? (1 mark)
   A. Nobody uses them
   B. It is easy to invent them correctly
   C. They are learned from speakers of the language
   D. Languages have no interjections

14. When copying a sentence, what should you check? (1 mark)
   A. Only the date
   B. Letter size, spacing, capital letter and full stop
   C. Only the colour of the pen
   D. Only the page number

15. What is a bargain? (1 mark)
   A. To sleep
   B. To discuss the price
   C. To steal
   D. To run

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
16. Write an advert of four sentences for hand-made baskets. Include a headline, two adjectives, a price and where to buy. (5 marks)

17. Complete with a preposition: The cat sleeps ______ the bed. (2 marks)

18. Write three instructions for what to do when it starts to rain at school. Use first, then and finally. (4 marks)

19. Complete with a simile: The baby slept like a ______. (2 marks)

20. Give two examples of constructive leisure activities. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #14 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. D — tipped
   Tipped shows what the pot did.

2. C — round
   Round describes shape.

3. A — Look at the audience and speak clearly
   Eye contact and clarity help.

4. A — Read it aloud
   Reading aloud shows if the order makes sense.

5. B — tiny
   Tiny describes size.

6. A — Short, like real speech
   Real conversations use short turns.

7. B — A stitch in time saves nine
   It is a short saying that gives advice.

8. D — Next
   Next shows the following step.

9. D — Yuck
   Yuck shows disgust.

10. D — A folder where proverbs are collected and kept
   A portfolio holds the class collection.

11. C — vote, count
   Vote and count are actions.

12. D — Before and
   A comma comes before the joining word.

13. C — They are learned from speakers of the language
   Ask real speakers for correct forms.

14. B — Letter size, spacing, capital letter and full stop
   These are the points of neat copying.

15. B — To discuss the price
   Bargaining is agreeing on price.

SECTION B
----
16. (5 marks)
   Answer: Any advert with a headline, two adjectives, a price and a place, for example: Strong Baskets for Sale. Our baskets are big and colourful. Only 300 shillings each. Buy at the market gate.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each of the four required features and one mark for clear sentences.

17. (2 marks)
   Answer: under (or on, if it sleeps on top)
   Working / marking points: One mark for a preposition and one for a sentence that makes sense.

18. (4 marks)
   Answer: First, go into the classroom. Then close the windows. Finally, wait for the rain to stop.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each clear instruction and one mark for using all three signal words.

19. (2 marks)
   Answer: log (or a stone, or any suitable comparison)
   Working / marking points: One mark for a suitable comparison and one for keeping like.

20. (2 marks)
   Answer: Reading, sports, drawing, singing, gardening, community service (any two).
   Working / marking points: One mark for each.
